title: Hosted API: region pinning and tenant-level data residency controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Implement tenant- and API-key-level region pinning for the Hosted API so customers can require that request processing and persisted artifacts (logs, cached KV prefixes, embeddings) remain within selected cloud regions. Deliverables: API surface for pinning, console settings, runtime routing enforcement, retention controls (default and overrides), audit/evidence artifact automation (scheduled reports + on-demand export), and migration tooling for existing tenants. Goals: satisfy regulatory requirements (data residency laws, contractual commitments), enable legal holds and retention proofs, and provide low-friction controls for customers to lock their workloads to specific regions without major latency regressions.
background: Customers in regulated verticals (fintech, healthcare, EU public sector) have asked for explicit enforcement that request processing and persisted data never leave a defined geography. Current Hosted API region routing is best-effort and optimized for latency; we need a deterministic pinning mechanism + retention and reporting to prove compliance for audits. This work must interoperate with Dedicated and Private offerings (consistent semantics) and integrate with our audit log and billing systems.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/keys/:id/region-pin accepts allowed_regions (list) and mode (strict|preferred), returns 200 and updates key metadata
Console: Organization and API-key settings UI to set default_region, allowed_regions, retention_days, legal_hold flag
Runtime: Router enforces strict pinning: requests for pinned keys are only routed to instances in allowed regions; non-compliant routings are blocked and generate an audit event

Persistence: All persisted artifacts (logs, embeddings, KV cache snapshots) for pinned keys are stored only in pinned regions; retention settings control auto-deletion and legal hold prevents deletion
Reporting: Automated weekly evidence bundle (signed manifest + CSV) available per tenant including retention state, region routing history, and deletion proofs; on-demand export within 24 hours
Observability: Metrics for region-deny counts, pinned-key traffic by region, and retention-policy violations available in Console and through API
Compatibility: Behavior documented and tested for cross-region fallback policies and integration with Dedicated/Private semantics
Security: Security review completed and implementation passes internal pen test for metadata exposure

migration_notes: For existing API keys: default to 'preferred' mode (best-effort routing) and surface an opt-in banner in Console. Provide a migration job that will verify existing persisted artifacts' locations and either copy or flag non-compliant objects. Offer a one-click bulk-enforce action with preview of affected data and estimated downtime. Customers can request a manual compliance migration assisted by Solutions Engineering.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): API + backend policy enforcement for new keys in 'preferred' mode; internal customers only. Phase 2 (beta): Console UX, retention UI, scheduled evidence bundles, opt-in migration for existing keys. Phase 3 (GA): strict mode enforcement, signed deletion receipts, 3rd-party SOC-ready reporting format. Monitor region-deny and error budgets, rollback toggle to disable strict enforcement per org in emergency.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: 1) Mode semantics: 'strict' blocks requests vs 'preferred' routes but logs; strict increases 5-15% of 99th latency on multi-region workloads. 2) Cross-region caching: do we allow ephemeral caching in non-pinned regions for latency? (proposal: no for strict, yes with TTL for preferred). 3) Evidence format: signed manifests provide cryptographic proof but increase storage and processing; need KMS integration. 4) Interaction with Dedicated: Dedicated tenants may require different enforcement hooks — require interface parity but implementation divergence.
testing_plan: Unit tests for API & policy engine, integration tests against multi-region staging cluster, retention e2e verifying deletion receipts and legal hold preservation, compliance e2e scenario for GDPR subject data removal with audit trail. Add synthetic tenants to load-test region-pin routing and measure latency/regression.
observability_and_sla: New metrics: pinned_key_request_deny_count, pinned_key_routed_by_region, retention_deletion_failures. Alerts: >1% deny rate for pinned keys, evidence bundle generation failures. SLO for weekly evidence bundle availability: 99.5%.
implementation_notes: Router will consult key metadata service on every request; cache metadata with 30s TTL and add policy-version header to trace. Storage layer will tag objects with region and owner key id; deletion jobs will produce a signed receipt using KMS per-tenant. Evidence bundles are tiled by day and include signed manifests + CSV summary. Consider quota implications for replication during migration.

risks: 1) Latency regressions in strict mode may push customers to unpin and reduce compliance value. 2) Incorrect migration could leave residual data in disallowed regions — require a strict verification pass. 3) KMS/keys lifecycle issues could invalidate deletion receipts; require rotation policy documentation.
